newsitem.title: HONG KONG: "Healthy" year start for Asia Pacific airlines.
newsitem.headline: "Healthy" year start for Asia Pacific airlines.

text.p: The Association of Asia-Pacific Airlines said its members made a positive start to the year with growth in both passenger and freight markets.

Its Orient Aviation magazine said "healthy" double digit growth continued in the cargo sector with freight tonne kilometres (FTKs) increasing 18.3 per cent in January and 12.0 per cent in February. Increases in capacity measured in FATKs were limited to 9.4 per cent in January and 3.3 per cent in February as members appeared to be trying to control over capacity, the magazine said.
The result was a 4.7 per cent and a 5.3 per cent rise in cargo load factor during the respective months over the same period in 1996 which were the biggest increases in two years.

The 18 members of AAPA, formerly the Orient Airlines Association, include leading Asian airlines such as Singapore Airlines, Cathay Pacific Airways Limited and Korean Air, also carried 6.1 percent more passengers in February and 8.2 per cent more in January compared to 1996.
